[size=150][b]Lionheart Fixt 0.25.1 - the startup crash[/b][/size]

[b]Install this over any earlier release. 0.19.0 through 0.25.0 could not reach the main menu.[/b]

Seven published releases. The game said so precisely, in its own diagnostic dialog, before the title
screen:

[i]The item we are looking for is [i]Skills/Fighting/Melee[/i] [...] It was referenced by[/i]
[i][i]Resources/Races/NPCs/Grace OMalley.Race:Skill Preset:Skill[/i][/i]

There is no [i]Skills/Fighting/Melee[/i] in Lionheart and there never was. The real skill is
[i]Skills/Fighting/OneHandedMelee[/i] -- which the crash dialog itself lists as item 9 of the skills it *did*
find, one line below the name it was looking for.

Grace O'Malley's race was authored in 0.19.0, during a review that found she could not have survived the
fight the act drops her into. The melee preset that fixed that named a skill that does not exist.

The engine resolves a race's skill presets [b]at load[/b], so this was not a latent defect waiting for the
right save. It was every launch, for everyone.

[b]The fix[/b]

One value in one file: [i]Melee[/i] becomes [i]OneHandedMelee[/i], keeping the preset of 110. Grace is what the
0.19.0 review intended -- 190 AC, 165 hit points, OneHandedMelee 110, Evasion 55.

[b]Why seven releases went out with it[/b]

[i]tools/validate.py[/i] resolves resource references and has done since early on; it is what caught the wrong
requirement paths during 0.22.0. It had two gaps, and they lined up exactly:

| gap | effect |
|---|---|
| it scanned only [i].dialogtree[/i], [i].zax[/i] and [i].can[/i] | [i].race[/i] files were [b]never[/b] examined |
| it had no reference kind for [i]Skill=[/i], [i]Race=[/i] or [i]Derived Character Attribute=[/i] | even a scanned race would not have had these checked |

Either gap alone would have caught this. Both together meant the one reference kind the engine kills the
process over was the one nothing looked at.

Both are closed. [i].race[/i] joins the scanned suffixes, and three kinds are added: [i]Skill=[/i] and
[i]Skill to select=[/i] resolving to [i].Skill[/i], [i]Derived Character Attribute=[/i] to [i].DerivedCharacterAttribute[/i],
and [i]Race=[/i] to [i].Race[/i] or [i].race[/i], since the shipped archive is inconsistent about that extension's case.

The check was then proved rather than assumed: reintroducing the exact bug makes the gate exit 1 with
*"Grace OMalley.Race: reference does not resolve to any file: 'Skills/Fighting/Melee'"*, and restoring
the fix makes it pass.

A sweep of all 279 Fixt resource files, across [b]376[/b] references of these kinds, found [b]exactly one[/b]
unresolved -- the one above. That sweep also covers the 36 derived-attribute references 0.25.0 added the
day before with its twelve thief races; they resolve, but until now nothing had proved it.

[b]The honest part[/b]

This is the failure mode the project's own standing trade makes likely: finish development, then
playtest. Nothing had been launched since 0.19.0, and [b]a crash before the main menu is invisible to
every gate that reads files rather than running them.[/b] Six releases of work were published on top of a
build that could not start.

Nothing in 0.19.0 through 0.25.0 is withdrawn or changed by this -- all of it was correct, and none of it
had ever run.

[b]Fixt[/b] is a cumulative restoration-and-repair mod for Lionheart, after Fallout Fixt.

Download, unzip, run [i]Mod Manager.bat[/i]. No save requirements: this one is a one-value repair and applies
to any character, including none. If you have any earlier release installed, replace it.

https://github.com/EricHype/LionheartFixt/releases/tag/v0.25.1
